query:
title: Go generated model rename

question: Our stable Go SDK has a model named A. I renamed the TypeSpec model to B and added @renamedFrom(Versions.v2, "A"), but regeneration still removes the exported Go type A. How can I keep the released Go type name?
ground_truth: Use a Go-scoped client name on the current TypeSpec model: @@clientName(B, "A", "go") in client.tsp. Regenerate and verify the public type remains A. The breaking-change guide explicitly identifies this @renamedFrom pattern as an exported-type rename that invalidates references to A; it prescribes clientName to restore the original name.

expected_references.title: Go breaking changes: model, enum, and union name changes

query:
title: Go field renamed after TypeSpec update

question: I renamed property a to b in my TypeSpec model Test and added @renamedFrom(Versions.v2, "a"). Our released Go struct has A, but regeneration replaces it with B. How do I keep A for Go without changing the other languages?
ground_truth: Apply @@clientName(Test.b, "a", "go") in client.tsp and regenerate. Target the current TypeSpec property Test.b; the Go-scoped name restores the original generated field A. Renaming the exported field otherwise breaks existing field access.

expected_references.title: Go breaking changes: property name changes

query:
title: Go enum value rename

question: In my TypeSpec enum Test, I renamed member a to b with @renamedFrom(Versions.v2, "a"). The wire value hasn't changed, but the generated Go constant name has. How can I retain the old Go name?
ground_truth: Apply @@clientName(Test.b, "a", "go") to the current TypeSpec enum member in client.tsp, then regenerate and check the resulting constant. Renaming an exported enum constant breaks callers referencing the old name even if the wire value stays the same. Target the source enum and member names, accounting for Go naming transformations.

expected_references.title: Go breaking changes: enum value name changes

testcase: Go property type change cannot be fixed by naming
query:
title: Go exported property type change

question: I used @typeChangedFrom to change a response property from string to int32. Our generated Go field now changes from *string to *int32. Can I fix that compatibility issue with a clientName customization?
ground_truth: No. The public field type change requires callers to change conversions or value handling. The Go breaking-change guide identifies this @typeChangedFrom pattern as breaking and says it cannot be resolved through client customizations. Restoring a name does not restore the old field type.

expected_references.title: Go breaking changes: property type changes

query:
title: Removed operation disappears from Go

question: I removed an operation from our new API version with @removed. Regeneration deletes the Go method our callers use. Can a client naming override recover the method?
ground_truth: No. Removing the operation removes the client method and breaks callers that invoke it. The Go guide lists operation deletion as a breaking change that cannot be resolved through client customizations. This is different from renaming an operation that still exists.

expected_references.title: Go breaking changes: operation deletion

query:
title: Added required Go operation parameter

question: My Go method used to take ctx, resourceName, and options. I added a required region parameter in the specification, and generation puts it before options. Why is this additive service feature source-breaking?
ground_truth: Existing calls do not supply the newly required argument, so they no longer match the method signature. The Go guide identifies required parameter addition as breaking and says it cannot be resolved through client customizations. An additive service capability is not necessarily an additive Go API change.

expected_references.title: Go breaking changes: required parameter addition

query:
title: Go response result type changes

question: I changed an operation's response body from string to int32 using @returnTypeChangedFrom. It still returns HTTP 200, but the Go response field changes from *string to *int32. Does retaining the status code preserve Go compatibility?
ground_truth: No. Changing the exported response field type breaks callers that read it, regardless of the HTTP status. The Go guide shows this @returnTypeChangedFrom pattern and says the resulting response-type break cannot be resolved through client customizations.

expected_references.title: Go breaking changes: response type changes

query:
title: Keep a synchronous method after an LRO change

question: I changed our service operation to a long-running template. The Go SDK now exposes BeginCreate and a poller instead of Create and its direct result. Can I just rename BeginCreate back to Create to preserve compatibility?
ground_truth: No. Switching to an LRO changes both the generated method name and its return shape, from a direct result to a poller. The Begin prefix is applied automatically. The Go guide classifies switching between synchronous and LRO forms as breaking and not resolvable through client customizations; a name alone cannot restore the old contract.

expected_references.title: Go breaking changes: long-running operation changes

testcase: Go operation rename review with scoped approval

title: HTTP approval and Go rename review

question: My ARM reviewers accepted an updateTags-to-update rename because its HTTP method and URI are unchanged. The Go reviewer still flagged the removed method, then approved after we explained the wider update body, versioning, and SDK mitigation options. Does that mean the rename was source-compatible?
ground_truth: No. The removed Go method is still a source-breaking change; ARM's HTTP-contract acceptance does not make old Go calls compile. In this case the Go reviewer accepted the explained change after the follow-up. Proceed under that scoped approval, without claiming the rename is compatible or that an additional naming fix was imposed as an unmet condition of the final approval.

testcase: Go accepted empty-model break before first GA
query:
title: Empty model removed before first GA

question: My preview Go SDK removes CalculateCostRequest, which is an empty model. Our service has not released its first GA SDK in any language. The Go owner has reviewed these facts. Can we take this particular break before first GA?
ground_truth: Yes. The expert accepted this specific break because CalculateCostRequest is empty and the service has not released its first GA package in any language. Keep that scoped rationale; it is not a general approval for all breaking changes in preview SDKs.

query:
title: Inherently fixed protocol values

question: I'm modeling an Azure API value that can only be IPv4 or IPv6. Is there any exception to the TypeSpec no-enum guidance, or must I always include string as an extensible variant?
ground_truth: The rule permits suppression when the set is inherently immutable, with IPv4 versus IPv6 as its example. For sets that can grow, use an open union containing the base scalar. A small set today is not enough by itself to justify treating it as immutable; versioning enums are also explicitly allowed.

expected_references.title: Azure core no-enum rule: suppression and versioning exceptions

query:
title: Follow-up within an explicit branch waiver

question: I have an example-correction follow-up to an already approved development-branch change. The Go owner explicitly said suppression would be added for the approved break and further changes to that release branch would not require approval. What should I do for this covered follow-up?
ground_truth: Use the explicitly granted arrangement: the approved breaking change receives suppression, and the covered release-branch follow-up does not need another approval. Do not reverse the owner's decision by requiring a new review for that same covered work. Keep the waiver limited to the associated work and release branch, not arbitrary future changes elsewhere.

query:
title: Go changelog uses a shortened model name

question: My TypeSpec model is WebPubSubSettings, but it appears as Settings in the Go changelog for package webpubsub. Which name should I target in client.tsp when I customize it for Go?
ground_truth: Target WebPubSubSettings, the actual TypeSpec model. The Go emitter trims a matching package-name prefix on a word boundary to avoid stuttering, so the generated Settings name is not the source symbol to customize. Inspect the regenerated Go name after applying the source customization.

expected_references.title: Go naming mechanisms: stuttering cut

testcase: Go LRO rename customization uses bare operation
query:
title: Preserve a renamed Go Begin method

question: I renamed our TypeSpec LRO from create to provision without changing its long-running behavior. The Go method changed from BeginCreate to BeginProvision. How should I preserve BeginCreate?
ground_truth: Customize the current source operation's bare name: @@clientName(provision, "create", "go"), qualified with its actual namespace or interface in client.tsp. The Go emitter adds Begin, so do not target BeginProvision or put BeginCreate in the override. Regenerate and verify BeginCreate. This addresses a rename, not a switch between synchronous and LRO behavior.

expected_references.title: Go naming mechanisms: list and LRO operation naming
Go breaking changes: operation name changes

testcase: Go pager rename customization uses bare operation

title: Preserve a renamed Go pager method

question: I renamed my paged TypeSpec operation listByResourceGroup to enumerateByResourceGroup, and Go replaced NewListByResourceGroupPager. The paging contract is unchanged. How can I retain the released method name?
ground_truth: Apply @@clientName(enumerateByResourceGroup, "listByResourceGroup", "go") to the current TypeSpec operation in client.tsp, using its actual qualification. The emitter supplies New and Pager, so customize the bare operation name rather than the generated method. Regenerate and check that NewListByResourceGroupPager remains. A paging-behavior change is a different, non-naming compatibility issue.

expected_references.title: Go naming mechanisms: list and LRO operation naming

query:
title: Set up client.tsp for Go customizations

question: I need Go-scoped client naming overrides. Where should I put client.tsp relative to main.tsp, which file imports which, and do I change the entry point in tspconfig.yaml?
ground_truth: Place client.tsp alongside main.tsp in the service specification directory. client.tsp becomes the client-generation entry point and imports main.tsp plus @azure-tools/typespec-client-generator-core; bring Azure.ClientGenerator.Core and your service namespace into scope. Do not import client.tsp from main.tsp, and do not modify the entry point in tspconfig.yaml. Put the supported Go-scoped customizations in client.tsp.

expected_references.title: Go breaking changes: client customization entry point and imports

query:

question: My Go SDK validation completed, and I want to inspect the generated artifacts rather than rely only on the status summary. Where do I find them, and are they always present after a failed run?

question: I'm adding github.com/coder/websocket to a Go SDK module that is neither azservicebus nor azeventhubs. I saw it allowed for those two modules. Is it part of the repository's general dependency allowance?
ground_truth: No. The standards list github.com/coder/websocket as an additional direct dependency for azservicebus and azeventhubs, not as a general allowance. ground_truth: Remove the locale code from the documentation link, then verify the resulting link works. The Go engineering-system guide says link verification checks both link validity and removal of locale codes such as en-us. A URL opening successfully does not by itself satisfy that check.

question: I'm coordinating retirement of the LambdaTest HyperExecute, Arize AI Observability Eval, Weights and Biases, and Pinecone Vector DB integrations. My draft only deprecates armweightsandbiases. Which Go packages should this retirement batch cover?
ground_truth: Cover all four modules: armlambdatesthyperexecute, armarizeaiobservabilityeval, armweightsandbiases, and armpineconevectordb. query:
title: Retire a module without retracting every version

question: I'm retiring our Go module in favor of a replacement. A teammate suggested retracting all old versions to announce the transition. Should I use retraction or deprecation, and where should the notices go?
ground_truth: Use module deprecation for retirement and migration. Retraction is for problematic module versions, not a synonym for retiring a module. The Go deprecation guide calls for a final patch with a // Deprecated: comment and migration instructions in go.mod, a CHANGELOG.md notice, and a README notice under the title. Put MIGRATION.md in the new module. Do not mass-retract otherwise usable versions merely to announce retirement.

testcase: Go sequential preview and GA release acceptance

question: I'm planning a preview API release with a feature, a first GA API release without it, and a later GA API release that adds it back. Our Go SDK changes go into main. Can I carry out these SDK releases one version after another?
ground_truth: Yes. The expert's guidance for this release plan was that proceeding one version after another is OK. Carry out the preview, first GA, and later GA in the intended sequence rather than combining their release work. This is acceptance of the sequencing described, not a claim that every unrelated breaking change is approved.

query:

question: My new major Go SDK design would use language capabilities requiring a newer compiler and drop compatibility with older compilers. Assuming the required compiler actually supports the design, can the owners accept this tradeoff if it improves long-term maintainability?
ground_truth: Yes. The owner feedback considered the proposed minimum-version increase reasonable on the assumption that it is a net win for the codebase's longevity, citing the earlier move for generics as precedent. Preserve that conditional acceptance. It does not verify a future compiler's feature availability or establish a universal minimum-Go policy; determine the actual supported compiler requirement separately.

testcase: Go distinguish REST and SDK breaking-change review stages
query:
title: Two breaking-change gates on my ARM specification

question: My specification change targets public main and has both BreakingChangeReviewRequired and BreakingChange-Go-Sdk labels. ARM review is also pending, and we have no branch-specific waiver. In what order should I complete these reviews and request merge?
ground_truth: First resolve the specification-level breaking-change review represented by BreakingChangeReviewRequired. Next complete ARM review and obtain ARM signoff. Then complete the Go SDK breaking-change review represented by BreakingChange-Go-Sdk, which follows the first two stages. Finally obtain PR approval and satisfy the merge requirements. Do not combine the REST specification and Go SDK gates or put all breaking-change approvals before ARM review.
